creators.name: Stephan Wensveen
creators.role: Professor of Constructive Design Research, Industrial Design, Eindhoven University of Technology
creators.bio: Stephan Wensveen studies how products couple action and function, and how research through design produces knowledge.
creators.why: He brings design-aesthetics and constructive design research theory to the study of designing with living organisms.
creators.role_zh: 埃因霍温理工大学工业设计系建构式设计研究教授
creators.bio_zh: Stephan Wensveen 研究产品如何把人的动作与功能联系起来，以及“通过设计做研究”如何产生知识。
creators.why_zh: 他把设计美学和建构式设计研究的理论带入“与生命一起设计”的研究。

creators.name: Ebba Ahlqvist
creators.role: Interaction design researcher, Chalmers University of Technology
creators.bio: Ebba Ahlqvist co-designed HoneyPot, a pair of networked plant pots that glow to connect two people at a distance.
creators.why: Her work shows a houseplant used as a quiet social link between people.
creators.role_zh: 查尔姆斯理工大学交互设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Ebba Ahlqvist 参与设计了 HoneyPot：一对联网的发光花盆，让相隔两地的人通过植物保持联系。
creators.why_zh: 她的作品把一盆室内植物变成人与人之间安静的社交纽带。

creators.name: Rachel Ann Arredondo
creators.role: Designer, Morphing Matter Lab (Carnegie Mellon University / UC Berkeley)
creators.bio: Rachel Ann Arredondo led Blue Ceramics, digitally fabricated morphing ceramic tiles co-designed with marine scientists to restore seagrass meadows.
creators.why: She applies shape-changing material design to ecological restoration.
creators.role_zh: Morphing Matter Lab 设计师（卡内基梅隆大学 / 加州大学伯克利分校）
creators.bio_zh: Rachel Ann Arredondo 主导了 Blue Ceramics：与海洋科学家共同设计、用数字制造做出的会变形的陶瓷砖，用于修复海草床。
creators.why_zh: 她把形变材料设计用在生态修复上。

creators.name: Andrea Bandoni
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Faculty of Fine Arts, University of Lisbon
creators.bio: Andrea Bandoni is a Brazilian designer who studies Amazonian craft and biofabrication with living trees.
creators.why: She links biodesign to ancestral, Indigenous making practices.
creators.role_zh: 里斯本大学美术学院设计师与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Andrea Bandoni 是巴西设计师，研究亚马孙的手工艺，以及借助活树进行的生物制造。
creators.why_zh: 她把生物设计与祖传的原住民制作方式联系起来。

creators.name: Riel Bessai
creators.role: Design researcher, Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering, TU Delft
creators.bio: Riel Bessai researches circular and more-than-human design, including the design of a festival stage attuned to local ecosystems.
creators.why: He proposes noticing and care as ways to design with the rhythms of other species.
creators.role_zh: 代尔夫特理工大学工业设计工程学院设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Riel Bessai 研究循环设计与超越人类的设计，其中包括一座顺应当地生态系统节律的音乐节舞台。
creators.why_zh: 他提出用“留意”和“照护”来顺应其他物种的节律进行设计。

creators.name: Fadi Botros
creators.role: HCI researcher, InnoVis group, University of Calgary (at the time of Go & Grow)
creators.bio: Fadi Botros built Go & Grow, a living plant that is watered according to its owner's physical activity.
creators.why: His study showed that a living visualisation creates pride, guilt and responsibility that charts do not.
creators.role_zh: 卡尔加里大学 InnoVis 组 HCI 研究者（Go & Grow 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Fadi Botros 做了 Go & Grow：一株根据主人运动量来浇水的活植物。
creators.why_zh: 他的研究表明，活的可视化能带来图表所没有的自豪、内疚和责任感。

creators.name: Jacqueline T. Chien
creators.role: HCI researcher, Cornell University (at the time of Biogotchi!)
creators.bio: Jacqueline T. Chien explored plants as living information displays by manipulating their growth to show personal data.
creators.why: Her Biogotchi! experiments are an early map of plant-based displays in HCI.
creators.role_zh: 康奈尔大学 HCI 研究者（Biogotchi! 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Jacqueline T. Chien 通过操控植物生长来显示个人数据，探索把植物当作活的信息显示器。
creators.why_zh: 她的 Biogotchi! 实验是 HCI 中植物显示器较早的一次系统探索。

creators.name: Ashley Colley
creators.role: Researcher, User Experience group, University of Lapland
creators.bio: Ashley Colley designs ambient and peripheral displays, including one that morphs the shadow of a houseplant.
creators.why: The plant-shadow display turns a plant's natural shadow into a calm information channel.
creators.role_zh: 拉普兰大学用户体验组研究者
creators.bio_zh: Ashley Colley 设计环境式与外围显示，其中一件作品改变室内植物的影子来传递信息。
creators.why_zh: 植物影子显示把植物天然的影子变成一种安静的信息通道。

creators.name: Till Fastnacht
creators.role: Media artist and researcher, Bauhaus-Universität Weimar (at the time of Sonnengarten)
creators.bio: Till Fastnacht co-created Sonnengarten, an urban light installation in which touching plants triggers light.
creators.why: The installation brings human-plant interaction into public urban space.
creators.role_zh: 包豪斯魏玛大学媒体艺术家与研究者（Sonnengarten 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Till Fastnacht 参与创作了 Sonnengarten：一件城市灯光装置，触摸植物就会点亮灯光。
creators.why_zh: 这件装置把人与植物的互动带进城市公共空间。

creators.name: Fernando Galdon
creators.role: Senior Tutor, Design Products, Royal College of Art
creators.bio: Fernando Galdon teaches and researches regenerative materials and furniture, framing their aesthetics as Bio-Brutalism.
creators.why: He names the raw, time-based aesthetics that appear when organisms help make objects.
creators.role_zh: 英国皇家艺术学院产品设计系高级导师
creators.bio_zh: Fernando Galdon 从事再生材料与家具的教学和研究，并把它们的美学概括为“Bio-Brutalism”（生物粗野主义）。
creators.why_zh: 他为生物参与制作时出现的粗粝、随时间变化的美学起了名字。

creators.name: Bingjie Gao
creators.role: Design researcher, Beijing Institute of Technology
creators.bio: Bingjie Gao co-designed Plant Playmate, a smart office plant with lights and expressions that offers short breaks from work stress.
creators.why: The project tests whether an interactive plant can support wellbeing at work.
creators.role_zh: 北京理工大学设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Bingjie Gao 参与设计了 Plant Playmate：一盆带灯光和表情的智能办公植物，帮助人在工作压力中小憩。
creators.why_zh: 该项目检验互动植物能否在工作中支持身心健康。

creators.name: Gabrielle Hong
creators.role: Design researcher, University of Sydney
creators.bio: Gabrielle Hong built a low-resolution display made of living moss that changes when sprayed with water.
creators.why: It explores living media as low-energy displays.
creators.role_zh: 悉尼大学设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Gabrielle Hong 用活苔藓做了一块低分辨率显示屏，喷水时它的样子会改变。
creators.why_zh: 它探索把活体媒介当作低能耗的显示器。

creators.name: Youyang Hu
creators.role: Researcher, Kakehi Lab, The University of Tokyo
creators.bio: Youyang Hu makes installations that read plant biosignals and render how plants experience wind, rain and light.
creators.why: His work treats plants as sensors of the environment and translates their responses into sound, light and VR.
creators.role_zh: 东京大学筧研究室研究者
creators.bio_zh: Youyang Hu 创作读取植物生物电信号的装置，把植物对风、雨和光的感受呈现出来。
creators.why_zh: 他把植物当作环境的感受者，把它们的反应转译成声音、光和虚拟现实。

creators.name: Leonardo Hummel
creators.role: Designer and researcher, University of Washington
creators.bio: Leonardo Hummel developed SeaWeaver, a method for building artificial reefs from hand-woven metal forms.
creators.why: He combines weaving craft with reef ecology to make conservation cheaper and easier to adopt.
creators.role_zh: 华盛顿大学设计师与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Leonardo Hummel 开发了 SeaWeaver：用手工编织的金属形体建造人工鱼礁的方法。
creators.why_zh: 他把编织手艺和鱼礁生态结合起来，让保护行动更便宜、更易推广。

creators.name: Sungjae Hwang
creators.role: HCI researcher, KAIST (at the time of My Green Pet)
creators.bio: Sungjae Hwang built My Green Pet, a plant that senses touch through small electrical currents and answers children with sounds and lights.
creators.why: It shows how touch sensing can make children see a plant as alive.
creators.role_zh: 韩国科学技术院 HCI 研究者（My Green Pet 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Sungjae Hwang 做了 My Green Pet：一株通过微弱电流感知触摸的植物，会用声音和灯光回应孩子。
creators.why_zh: 它展示了触摸感应如何让孩子意识到植物是活的。

creators.name: Naohiro Isokawa
creators.role: Researcher, Keio University Shonan Fujisawa Campus
creators.bio: Naohiro Isokawa designs aquarium systems that sense fish and tank conditions and show them as speech bubbles.
creators.why: His TalkingNemo and AffectiveNemo are early animal-computer interaction work on pet fish.
creators.role_zh: 庆应义塾大学湘南藤泽校区研究者
creators.bio_zh: Naohiro Isokawa 设计水族箱系统：感知鱼和水体状况，再用对话气泡显示出来。
creators.why_zh: 他的 TalkingNemo 和 AffectiveNemo 是针对观赏鱼的早期动物-计算机交互研究。

creators.name: Riku Iwasaki
creators.role: Researcher, Digital Nature Group, University of Tsukuba
creators.bio: Riku Iwasaki developed Silk fabricator, which guides silkworms to spin flat silk sheets over computer-designed forms.
creators.why: It treats silkworms as a fabrication process, not only as a source of thread.
creators.role_zh: 筑波大学 Digital Nature Group 研究者
creators.bio_zh: Riku Iwasaki 开发了 Silk fabricator：引导蚕在计算机设计的形体上吐出平面丝片。
creators.why_zh: 它把蚕当作一种制造工艺，而不只是丝的来源。

creators.name: Yoichi Ochiai
creators.role: Associate Professor, University of Tsukuba; head of Digital Nature Group
creators.bio: Yoichi Ochiai is a media artist and researcher whose lab works on computational fabrication, holography and insect-based interfaces.
creators.why: His group repeatedly uses living insects (silkworms, cockroaches) as parts of fabrication and display systems.
creators.role_zh: 筑波大学副教授，Digital Nature Group 负责人
creators.bio_zh: Yoichi Ochiai（落合阳一）是媒体艺术家与研究者，他的实验室研究计算制造、全息和以昆虫为基础的界面。
creators.why_zh: 他的团队多次把活昆虫（蚕、蟑螂）用作制造和显示系统的一部分。

creators.name: Sylvia Janicki
creators.role: PhD researcher, Digital Media, Georgia Institute of Technology
creators.bio: Sylvia Janicki makes interactive installations with plants and biosensors about landscape, colonial history and more-than-human relations.
creators.why: Sensing Bodies brings postcolonial critique into plant-based interaction design.
creators.role_zh: 佐治亚理工学院数字媒体博士研究者
creators.bio_zh: Sylvia Janicki 用植物和生物传感器创作互动装置，关注地景、殖民历史与超越人类的关系。
creators.why_zh: Sensing Bodies 把后殖民批判带进植物交互设计。

creators.name: Michi Kanda
creators.role: Researcher, Keio University Graduate School of Media Design
creators.bio: Michi Kanda designed a plant whose grow light is driven by the owner's eye-blink fatigue data.
creators.why: The work couples human biosignals with plant health as a mirror for wellbeing.
creators.role_zh: 庆应义塾大学媒体设计研究科研究者
creators.bio_zh: Michi Kanda 设计了一盆植物：它的补光灯由主人的眨眼疲劳数据控制。
creators.why_zh: 这件作品把人的生理信号与植物健康连在一起，映照人的状态。

creators.name: Haruka Kasuga
creators.role: Researcher, Hokkaido University
creators.bio: Haruka Kasuga studies science communication with VR, including videos that simulate how turtles, geckos and frogs see.
creators.why: The work gives people a mediated taste of other animals' vision.
creators.role_zh: 北海道大学研究者
creators.bio_zh: Haruka Kasuga 研究用虚拟现实做科学传播，包括模拟乌龟、壁虎和青蛙视觉的影像。
creators.why_zh: 这项工作让人以间接方式体验其他动物的视觉。

creators.name: Donghyeon Ko
creators.role: HCI researcher, Department of Industrial Design, KAIST
creators.bio: Donghyeon Ko designed BubbleTalk, which turns a person's actions near a fish tank into bubbles inside it.
creators.why: It looks at fishkeeping as a relationship and gives the human a way to reach the fish.
creators.role_zh: 韩国科学技术院工业设计系 HCI 研究者
creators.bio_zh: Donghyeon Ko 设计了 BubbleTalk：把人在鱼缸旁的动作转化成缸里的气泡。
creators.why_zh: 它把养鱼看作一种关系，给人一种“够得着”鱼的方式。

creators.name: Satoshi Kuribayashi
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Keio University SFC (at the time of I/O Plant)
creators.bio: Satoshi Kuribayashi created I/O Plant and Plant Feeling Light, toolkits and lamps that treat plants as input and output modules.
creators.why: His 2007 toolkit is one of the earliest plant-interface kits in HCI.
creators.role_zh: 庆应义塾大学湘南藤泽校区设计师与研究者（I/O Plant 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Satoshi Kuribayashi 创作了 I/O Plant 和 Plant Feeling Light：把植物当作输入输出模块的工具包和灯具。
creators.why_zh: 他 2007 年的工具包是 HCI 中最早的植物界面套件之一。

creators.name: Qiuyu Lu
creators.role: PhD researcher, Morphing Matter Lab (Carnegie Mellon University / UC Berkeley)
creators.bio: Qiuyu Lu designs plant-facing sensors and shape-changing materials, including a wearable paper chip that reads plant guttation droplets.
creators.why: The Guttation Sensor lets people read plant chemistry on site.
creators.role_zh: Morphing Matter Lab 博士研究者（卡内基梅隆大学 / 加州大学伯克利分校）
creators.bio_zh: Qiuyu Lu 设计面向植物的传感器和形变材料，包括一张能读取植物吐水液滴的可穿戴纸芯片。
creators.why_zh: Guttation Sensor 让人能在现场读懂植物的化学信号。

creators.name: Tyler Luong
creators.role: Engineering researcher, Bucknell University
creators.bio: Tyler Luong tested plant and mud microbial fuel cells as power sources for low-power plant sensors.
creators.why: The work explores sensing systems powered by the plants and microbes they monitor.
creators.role_zh: 巴克内尔大学工程研究者
creators.bio_zh: Tyler Luong 测试用植物与泥土微生物燃料电池为低功耗植物传感器供电。
creators.why_zh: 这项工作探索由被监测的植物和微生物自己供电的传感系统。

creators.name: Julia Moser
creators.role: Textile designer and researcher, University of Arts Linz
creators.bio: Julia Moser dyes textiles with living pigment-producing bacteria and develops ways to design patterns with them.
creators.why: She turns bacterial dyeing from a single effect into a pattern-design method.
creators.role_zh: 林茨艺术大学纺织设计师与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Julia Moser 用会产生色素的活细菌给织物染色，并研究如何用它们设计图案。
creators.why_zh: 她把细菌染色从单一效果发展成一种图案设计方法。

creators.name: Hye Yeon Nam
creators.role: Associate Professor of Digital Art, Louisiana State University
creators.bio: Hye Yeon Nam is a media artist whose recent work, including FloraWear, puts living plants on the body.
creators.why: FloraWear is a DIY kit for wearing and caring for a plant every day.
creators.role_zh: 路易斯安那州立大学数字艺术副教授
creators.bio_zh: Hye Yeon Nam 是媒体艺术家，近期作品（包括 FloraWear）把活植物戴在身上。
creators.why_zh: FloraWear 是一套可以自己动手做、每天佩戴并照料植物的套件。

creators.name: Daniëlle Ooms
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Industrial Design, Eindhoven University of Technology
creators.bio: Daniëlle Ooms designed a toolkit for collecting mud to power Electric Life, a bacteria-powered light installation by Teresa van Dongen.
creators.why: Her reflection moves biodesign from concern for use to care for the microbes.
creators.role_zh: 埃因霍温理工大学工业设计系设计师与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Daniëlle Ooms 为 Teresa van Dongen 的细菌供电灯光装置 Electric Life 设计了一套采集泥土的工具包。
creators.why_zh: 她的反思把生物设计从“关注用途”推向“照护微生物”。

creators.name: Raul Pereira Pinto
creators.role: Design researcher, University of Aveiro
creators.bio: Raul Pereira Pinto worked on objects built by honeybees as creative agents in design.
creators.why: The project treats bees as co-makers in the creative industries.
creators.role_zh: 阿威罗大学设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Raul Pereira Pinto 研究由蜜蜂作为设计中的创作主体所筑造的物件。
creators.why_zh: 该项目把蜜蜂当作创意产业中的共同制作者。

creators.name: Serena Pollastri
creators.role: Lecturer in Design, ImaginationLancaster, Lancaster University
creators.bio: Serena Pollastri researches design for more-than-human cities and visual tools for multispecies futures.
creators.why: Her group visualises what urban places are like for nonhuman life, such as light and ultrasound at a dock.
creators.role_zh: 兰卡斯特大学 ImaginationLancaster 设计讲师
creators.bio_zh: Serena Pollastri 研究面向超越人类城市的设计，以及想象多物种未来的视觉工具。
creators.why_zh: 她的团队把城市场所对非人类生命意味着什么（例如码头上的光与超声）可视化。

creators.name: Aidan Mark Puse
creators.role: Interaction design student, University of Sydney (at the time of Synthium)
creators.bio: Aidan Mark Puse co-designed Synthium, an installation that turns electrical signals from mushrooms into sound in urban green spaces.
creators.why: It invites passers-by to play with fungi as fellow city dwellers.
creators.role_zh: 悉尼大学交互设计学生（Synthium 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Aidan Mark Puse 参与设计了 Synthium：在城市绿地里把蘑菇的电信号变成声音的装置。
creators.why_zh: 它邀请路人把真菌当作城市里的邻居来玩。

creators.name: Silvia Ruzanka
creators.role: Artist and Lecturer, Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
creators.bio: Silvia Ruzanka is a media artist who makes games and glitch art, including a videogame played by a Venus flytrap.
creators.why: Plant Play asks what play means for a nonhuman player.
creators.role_zh: 伦斯勒理工学院艺术家与讲师
creators.bio_zh: Silvia Ruzanka 是媒体艺术家，创作游戏和故障艺术，其中包括一款由捕蝇草来玩的电子游戏。
creators.why_zh: Plant Play 追问：对非人类玩家来说，“玩”意味着什么。

creators.name: Elena Sabinson
creators.role: Designer and researcher, Cornell University
creators.bio: Elena Sabinson designs soft robotic surfaces and interiors, including pheB, which moves in response to a plant's signals.
creators.why: pheB turns plant biofeedback into a breathing surface for people in confined spaces.
creators.role_zh: 康奈尔大学设计师与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Elena Sabinson 设计软体机器人表面与室内环境，其中 pheB 会随植物的信号而运动。
creators.why_zh: pheB 把植物生物反馈变成一面会“呼吸”的墙面，服务于处在封闭空间中的人。

creators.name: Takumi Saeki
creators.role: Artist and researcher, Kyushu University
creators.bio: Takumi Saeki prints images with bioluminescent bacteria as ink, so the image glows, fades and disappears as the bacteria live and die.
creators.why: His work makes a media image depend on a microbial life cycle.
creators.role_zh: 九州大学艺术家与研究者
creators.bio_zh: Takumi Saeki 用发光细菌作墨水印制图像，图像随细菌的生长与死亡而发光、衰退并消失。
creators.why_zh: 他的作品让一幅媒体图像依附于微生物的生命周期。

creators.name: Olivia Seow
creators.role: Designer and researcher, MIT Media Lab (at the time of Pudica)
creators.bio: Olivia Seow proposed Pudica, a framework for plant-based interfaces built around the touch-sensitive Mimosa pudica.
creators.why: It lists what designers must handle (maintenance, reproducibility) when a plant is the display.
creators.role_zh: MIT 媒体实验室设计师与研究者（Pudica 时期）
creators.bio_zh: Olivia Seow 提出了 Pudica：以含羞草为核心的植物界面设计框架。
creators.why_zh: 它列出了把植物当显示器时设计者必须处理的问题（维护、可复现性）。

creators.name: Fei (Dillon) Shieh
creators.role: Design researcher, Eindhoven University of Technology
creators.bio: Fei (Dillon) Shieh co-designed Minty Zoo, a cabinet of sensed mint plants whose water and light are redistributed by their collective behaviour.
creators.why: It gives plants a say in how resources are shared.
creators.role_zh: 埃因霍温理工大学设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Fei (Dillon) Shieh 参与设计了 Minty Zoo：一个装有薄荷的柜子，传感器读取植物的集体行为，再据此重新分配水和光。
creators.why_zh: 它让植物对资源如何分配“有发言权”。

creators.name: Yuichiro Takeuchi
creators.role: Researcher, Sony Computer Science Laboratories
creators.bio: Yuichiro Takeuchi works on digital fabrication for cities and ecologies, including 3D-printed hydroponic landscapes.
creators.why: Printable Hydroponics proposes printing whole ecological systems, not just objects.
creators.role_zh: 索尼计算机科学研究所研究员
creators.bio_zh: Yuichiro Takeuchi 研究面向城市与生态的数字制造，包括 3D 打印的水培地景。
creators.why_zh: Printable Hydroponics 提出打印整个生态系统，而不只是物件。

creators.name: Yuga Tsukuda
creators.role: Researcher, Digital Nature Group, University of Tsukuba
creators.bio: Yuga Tsukuda develops Calmbots, cockroaches with small backpacks steered as a swarm to draw, carry and display.
creators.why: Calmbots turns insects into a shared, reprogrammable interface.
creators.role_zh: 筑波大学 Digital Nature Group 研究者
creators.bio_zh: Yuga Tsukuda 开发了 Calmbots：背着小型背包的蟑螂，以群体方式被引导去绘画、搬运和显示。
creators.why_zh: Calmbots 把昆虫变成一种可以反复编程的共享界面。

creators.name: Peter Washington
creators.role: Researcher, Riedel-Kruse Lab, Stanford University (at the time of the work)
creators.bio: Peter Washington built a JavaScript API and online IDE for programming games and experiments with live Euglena under remote microscopes.
creators.why: It makes biotic game prototyping as easy as writing a web app.
creators.role_zh: 斯坦福大学 Riedel-Kruse 实验室研究者（当时）
creators.bio_zh: Peter Washington 开发了 JavaScript API 和在线编程环境，让人通过远程显微镜用活的眼虫编写游戏与实验。
creators.why_zh: 它让制作生物游戏原型像写网页一样容易。

creators.name: Xinquan Wen
creators.role: Design researcher, School of Design, Hong Kong Polytechnic University
creators.bio: Xinquan Wen designed Sloooooooooow, a smart home in which curtains move with the humidity that plants transpire.
creators.why: The work proposes a plant-decentred view: design for the shared microclimate, not the single plant.
creators.role_zh: 香港理工大学设计学院设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Xinquan Wen 设计了 Sloooooooooow：一个智能家居装置，窗帘随植物蒸腾带来的湿度变化而移动。
creators.why_zh: 这件作品提出“去植物中心”的视角：为共享的微气候设计，而不是为单株植物设计。

creators.name: Siyu Yao
creators.role: Artist and designer, Musashino Art University
creators.bio: Siyu Yao makes silk installations from flat cocoons, where silkworms spin planar sheets instead of 3D cocoons.
creators.why: The work revives a Showa-era technique that keeps the silkworm alive.
creators.role_zh: 武藏野美术大学艺术家与设计师
creators.bio_zh: Siyu Yao 用平面茧创作丝织装置：蚕吐出的是平面丝片，而不是立体的茧。
creators.why_zh: 这件作品复兴了昭和时期一种让蚕得以存活的技艺。

creators.name: Ying Zhou
creators.role: Design researcher, Zhejiang University
creators.bio: Ying Zhou co-designed MossWater, a moss display that is watered when office workers drink water.
creators.why: It uses care for moss as a metaphor for caring for one's own health.
creators.role_zh: 浙江大学设计研究者
creators.bio_zh: Ying Zhou 参与设计了 MossWater：办公室员工每喝一次水，苔藓显示器就被浇一次水。
creators.why_zh: 它用照料苔藓来比喻照顾自己的健康。

works.title: Aesthetics in Designing with the Living
works.description: A two-part systematic review: it first distils three orientations of 'critical aesthetics' from 39 texts on more-than-human, posthuman and multispecies aesthetics, then codes 83 HCI and design artefacts made with living organisms against them.
works.description_zh: 一篇两部分的系统综述：先从 39 篇讨论超越人类、后人类与多物种美学的文献中提炼出“批判美学”的三种取向，再用它们对 83 件用活体生物做的 HCI 与设计作品进行编码分析。
works.idea_en: Aesthetics in designing with the living is not only how an artefact looks to people: it also covers how other beings sense, how we relate to them, and what ethical and political questions the work raises.
works.idea_zh: 与生命一起设计时，美学不只是作品在人眼里的样子，还包括其他生命如何感知、人与它们如何相处，以及作品提出了哪些伦理和政治问题。
works.method: Study I reviewed Google Scholar literature on critical aesthetics; Study II screened 4,252 ACM DL, DRS and IJDesign articles down to 88 papers and 83 artefact sets, coded for mediation of nonhuman senses (C1), relational engagement (C2) and ethico-political provocation (C3).
works.method_zh: 研究一梳理 Google Scholar 上关于批判美学的文献；研究二从 ACM DL、DRS 与 IJDesign 的 4252 篇文章中筛出 88 篇论文、83 组作品，按“非人类感知的中介”（C1）、“关系性的参与”（C2）和“伦理政治挑衅”（C3）三类编码。

paper.title: Aesthetics in Designing with the Living: A Systematic Review of Critical Perspectives and Artefacts

works.title: HoneyPot
works.description: Two networked plant pots that glow with warm ambient light; touching one lights up its remote twin, so two people living apart can feel each other's presence through their plants.
works.description_zh: 两只联网的花盆会发出温暖的环境光；触碰其中一只，远方的另一只也会亮起，让分隔两地的人通过各自的植物感到彼此的存在。
works.idea_en: A houseplant can be a slow, calm channel for social connection.
works.idea_zh: 一盆室内植物可以成为缓慢而平静的社交通道。
works.method: Sensor-equipped pots with LEDs are linked over the internet; the design was iterated through prototypes and tested with adolescents facing isolation.
works.method_zh: 装有传感器和 LED 的花盆通过网络互联；经过多轮原型迭代，并与面临孤独问题的青少年一起测试。

paper.title: HoneyPot: Connecting Through a Mediated Ambient Plant

works.title: Blue Ceramics
works.description: Digitally fabricated ceramic tiles that morph during firing into shapes that shelter seagrass seeds and trap sediment, designed with marine scientists for restoring seagrass meadows.
works.description_zh: 用数字制造做出的陶瓷砖，在烧制中变形为能保护海草种子、截留沉积物的形状，是与海洋科学家一起为修复海草床设计的。
works.idea_en: Design the material with the ecosystem: let the seabed's currents, seeds and sediment set the form.
works.idea_zh: 和生态系统一起设计材料：让海底的水流、种子和沉积物决定形态。
works.method: Printed clay patterns shrink unevenly in the kiln so flat tiles curl into 3D forms; geometries were iterated in Grasshopper against seagrass seed and sediment behaviour described by scientists.
works.method_zh: 打印的黏土图案在窑中不均匀收缩，让平板卷曲成立体形态；形体在 Grasshopper 中迭代，依据科学家描述的海草种子与沉积物行为来调整。

paper.title: Blue Ceramics: Co-designing Morphing Ceramics for Seagrass Meadow Restoration

works.title: Biofabrication with cuia fruits
works.description: A design study that shapes objects while they grow on the calabash tree (Crescentia cujete), whose fruits Amazonian artisans have long turned into bowls called cuias.
works.description_zh: 一项设计研究：趁葫芦树（Crescentia cujete）的果实还长在树上时就为它们塑形；亚马孙手工艺人历来用这种果实做成名为 cuia 的碗。
works.idea_en: Biofabrication can start from ancestral craft: the tree grows the object, the designer guides it.
works.idea_zh: 生物制造可以从祖传手艺出发：树把物件长出来，设计师只做引导。
works.method: Historical research, interviews with traditional artisans and hands-on trials with living cuieira trees in a bioeconomy setting, shaping fruits during growth.
works.method_zh: 结合历史研究、对传统手艺人的访谈，以及在生物经济场景中对活的 cuieira 树进行的实验，在果实生长过程中为其塑形。

paper.title: Collaborating with an Amazonian tree: a bio-product design experiment with ancestral references

works.title: Designing with more-than-human temporalities (festival stage)
works.description: The design and construction of a music festival stage in France, used to show how designers can attend to the rhythms of insects and the local ecosystem rather than to a fixed project timeline.
works.description_zh: 在法国设计并搭建一座音乐节舞台，借此说明设计师如何顺应昆虫与当地生态系统的节律，而不是只盯着固定的项目时间表。
works.idea_en: Noticing and care let other species' time scales into the design process.
works.idea_zh: “留意”与“照护”能把其他物种的时间尺度带进设计过程。
works.method: A reflective case study of the stage's conceptualisation and build, analysed through two practices: noticing and care.
works.method_zh: 对舞台从构思到建造的过程做反思性案例研究，并从“留意”和“照护”两种实践来分析。

paper.title: Designing with more-than-human temporalities

works.title: Go & Grow
works.description: A living plant that receives water in proportion to how active its owner is: the fitter the owner, the healthier the plant. Ten people lived with one for six weeks.
works.description_zh: 一株活植物，获得的水量与主人的运动量成正比：主人越活跃，植物越健康。十位参与者与它共处了六周。
works.idea_en: A living visualisation makes data personal: people feel pride, guilt and responsibility toward the plant.
works.idea_zh: 活的可视化让数据变得切身：人会对植物感到自豪、内疚和责任。
works.method: A fitness tracker's step data drives a pump that waters the plant; a six-week qualitative study led to a Goal Motivation Model.
works.method_zh: 运动手环的步数数据控制水泵为植物浇水；六周的质性研究得出了一个“目标激励模型”。

paper.title: Go and Grow: Mapping Personal Data to a Living Plant

works.title: Biogotchi!
works.description: Four experiments that manipulate how plants grow, bend and colour to display personal data, such as a person's behaviour, as ambiguous, living feedback.
works.description_zh: 四组实验通过操控植物的生长、弯曲和颜色来显示个人数据（例如人的行为），形成含混而有生命的反馈。
works.idea_en: Plants can be slow, affective displays for personal information.
works.idea_zh: 植物可以成为缓慢而带情感的个人信息显示器。
works.method: A plant-manipulation system controls light, water and other conditions so that growth changes encode data; four experiments test the design space.
works.method_zh: 一套植物操控系统调节光照、水分等条件，让生长变化编码数据；四组实验探索这一设计空间。

paper.title: Biogotchi! An Exploration of Plant-Based Information Displays

works.title: Plant shadow morphing display
works.description: An ambient display that changes the shadow cast by a real houseplant to carry low-priority notifications.
works.description_zh: 一种环境式显示：改变真实室内植物投下的影子，用来传递不那么紧急的通知。
works.idea_en: A plant's natural shadow can carry information without adding another screen.
works.idea_zh: 植物天然的影子就能承载信息，不必再多一块屏幕。
works.method: A projector adds or removes shadow shapes around the shadow of a real plant lit by a desk lamp; a focus group (n = 6) discussed the concept.
works.method_zh: 台灯照亮真实植物，投影仪在它的影子周围增减阴影形状；一个 6 人焦点小组讨论了这一概念。

paper.title: Plant shadow morphing as a peripheral display

works.title: Sonnengarten
works.description: An urban light installation in Weimar: plants set in a tilted glowing planter respond to passers-by's touch with light.
works.description_zh: 魏玛的一件城市灯光装置：种在倾斜发光花槽里的植物，被路人触摸时会以灯光回应。
works.idea_en: Make plants in a city square noticeable by letting them answer touch.
works.idea_zh: 让植物回应触摸，使城市广场上的植物被人注意到。
works.method: Capacitive sensing through the plants detects touch and triggers LED light patterns in the planter.
works.method_zh: 通过植物进行电容感应检测触摸，触发花槽里的 LED 灯光变化。

paper.title: Sonnengarten: urban light installation with human-plant interaction

works.title: Worm Stool
works.description: A stool by William Eliot cast from the tunnels that mealworms eat through polystyrene; sugar water injected into the block steers where they chew.
works.description_zh: William Eliot 设计的一张凳子，形体取自黄粉虫啃穿聚苯乙烯留下的隧道；向泡沫块中注射糖水，引导它们往哪里啃。
works.idea_en: Let animal behaviour carve the form, then scale it up: the object records how the insects responded.
works.idea_zh: 让动物的行为雕刻形体，再把它放大：物件记录了昆虫的反应。
works.method: Mealworms eat through polystyrene guided by sugar-water injections; the paths are cast in wax and scaled up to a full-size stool.
works.method_zh: 黄粉虫在糖水引导下啃食聚苯乙烯；把形成的通道用蜡翻模，再放大成真实尺寸的凳子。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating behaviour into sculpture

paper.title: Bio-Brutalism; five case studies framing the emergence of new raw aesthetics at the intersection of material regeneration, environmental design, and craft

works.title: Plant Playmate
works.description: A smart office plant with interactive lights, anthropomorphic facial expressions and virtual credits, tested as a way to take short stress-relief breaks at work.
works.description_zh: 一盆智能办公植物，带互动灯光、拟人表情和虚拟积分，用来测试能否帮助人在工作中短暂放松。
works.idea_en: An interactive plant can make micro-breaks more pleasant than an ordinary plant.
works.idea_zh: 互动植物能让工间小憩比普通植物更愉快。
works.method: A within-subject study with 18 office workers compared it with an ordinary plant using electrodermal data, SAM and UEQ questionnaires and interviews.
works.method_zh: 对 18 位办公人员做被试内实验，与普通植物对比，采集皮电数据、SAM 与 UEQ 问卷和访谈。

paper.title: Plant Playmate: exploring effects of interactive plants for mental wellness microbreaks during knowledge-based work

works.title: Raaz
works.description: A bioart project that encoded a Persian Sufi poem by Hafez into the DNA of living yeast and used the yeast to brew 'poetry-infused wine'.
works.description_zh: 一件生物艺术作品：把哈菲兹的一首波斯苏菲诗编码进活酵母的 DNA，再用这种酵母酿出“注入诗歌的葡萄酒”。
works.idea_en: Synthetic biology can carry culture: the work brings Islamic and Persian associations of wine into a Western-dominated bioart field.
works.idea_zh: 合成生物学也能承载文化：作品把伊斯兰与波斯文化中关于酒的意涵带入以西方为主导的生物艺术领域。
works.method: The poem was converted to Morse code and then to DNA sequences, inserted into yeast cells and fermented; the paper pairs this with interviews with expert bioartists.
works.method_zh: 诗句先转成摩尔斯电码，再转成 DNA 序列，插入酵母细胞后发酵；论文还结合了对资深生物艺术家的访谈。

paper.title: “Turning the Invisible Visible”: Transdisciplinary Bioart Explorations in Human-DNA Interaction

works.title: Sprayful Interaction
works.description: A slow, low-resolution display made of living moss panels: spraying water makes dry, curled moss open up and turn green, so people 'draw' by watering.
works.description_zh: 一块由活苔藓板组成的慢速低分辨率显示屏：喷水后，干燥卷曲的苔藓会舒展变绿，人们用浇水来“作画”。
works.idea_en: A living display can use almost no electricity: water is the pixel driver.
works.idea_zh: 活的显示器几乎不耗电：水就是像素的驱动器。
works.method: Moss boards pinned to a wall in a design school respond to a spray gun; ten participants took part in think-aloud sessions, observation and interviews.
works.method_zh: 设计学院墙上钉着苔藓板，用喷壶喷水驱动变化；10 位参与者参加了出声思考、观察和访谈。

paper.title: Sprayful Interaction: Perceptions of a Moss-based SLow-resolution Living Media Display

works.title: Synplant
works.description: An installation of plant sensing units that reads plants' biosignals as wind and rain hit them and turns these responses into cymatics patterns of light and sound.
works.description_zh: 一件由多个植物传感单元组成的装置：读取植物在风吹雨打时的生物电信号，把这些反应转成光与声的“声流形”（cymatics）图案。
works.idea_en: Experience the weather from a plant's point of view.
works.idea_zh: 从植物的角度去感受天气。
works.method: Supervised learning (SVM/SVR) classifies changes in plant biopotential under environmental stimuli and drives acoustic-lighting devices that vibrate water into cymatics patterns.
works.method_zh: 用监督学习（SVM/SVR）识别植物生物电在环境刺激下的变化，并驱动声光装置让水面振出声流形图案。

paper.title: Synplant: Cymatics Visualization of Plant-Environment Interaction Based on Plants Biosignals

works.title: Immersive Flora
works.description: A VR forest built from 3D scans in which particle effects move with what real forest plants are sensing: their biosignals are classified as responses to wind, rain and sunlight.
works.description_zh: 一个由三维扫描重建的虚拟森林，其中的粒子效果随真实林中植物的感受而变化：它们的生物电信号被识别为对风、雨和阳光的反应。
works.idea_en: Let people feel the forest's weather through what the plants perceive.
works.idea_zh: 让人通过植物的感知去体会森林里的天气。
works.method: Biosensors on plants in a forest observation station feed machine-learning classifiers; results drive a real-time point-cloud particle system of the reconstructed forest.
works.method_zh: 森林观测站里植物上的生物传感器把数据送入机器学习分类器，结果实时驱动重建森林的点云粒子系统。

paper.title: Immersive Flora: Re-Engaging with the Forest through the Visualisation of Plant-Environment Interactions in Virtual Reality

works.title: SeaWeaver
works.description: Artificial reef units made by hand-weaving metal into complex wreath-like forms that give fish and coral the crevices and surfaces a natural reef offers; pilots ran for three years.
works.description_zh: 用手工编织金属做成花环般复杂形体的人工鱼礁单元，为鱼和珊瑚提供天然礁石那样的缝隙与附着面；试点已运行三年。
works.idea_en: Weaving craft can produce reef-like complexity cheaply and at scale.
works.idea_zh: 编织手艺能以低成本、可推广的方式做出类似礁石的复杂结构。
works.method: Parametric weaving patterns produce complex geometries; simple electrochemical processes add corrosion resistance and help mineral growth on the structures.
works.method_zh: 参数化的编织图案生成复杂几何；简单的电化学处理提高耐腐蚀性，并促进矿物在结构上生长。

paper.title: SeaWeaver: Integrating Cultural Craft and Materials Innovation for Artificial Reef Conservation Strategies

works.title: My Green Pet
works.description: An interactive plant for children that recognises stroking, tickling and holding through tiny currents and answers with laughter, cries and lights, as if it had feelings.
works.description_zh: 一株给孩子的互动植物：通过微弱电流识别抚摸、挠痒和握住等动作，并以笑声、哭声和灯光回应，仿佛它有情绪。
works.idea_en: Personifying a plant helps children understand that plants are alive.
works.idea_zh: 把植物拟人化，能帮助孩子理解植物是活的。
works.method: A current-based sensing framework on an Arduino classifies touch gestures on a regular potted plant and plays voice files and LED feedback; a user test with children followed.
works.method_zh: 基于 Arduino 的电流感应框架识别普通盆栽上的触摸手势，播放语音并点亮 LED；随后与儿童进行了用户测试。

paper.title: My Green Pet: a current-based interactive plant for children

works.title: Negotiating with the Garden (Beehouse)
works.description: A designer builds a beehouse for red mason bees in his own garden and lets the bees' nesting season set the pace of making, then designs an artefact that conveys being 'not in control'.
works.description_zh: 设计师在自家花园为红壁蜂建造蜂屋，让蜜蜂的筑巢季节决定制作节奏，随后又设计了一件传达“不在掌控之中”感受的作品。
works.idea_en: Design for interdependence: bees, weather, plants, materials and the designer share one schedule.
works.idea_zh: 为相互依存而设计：蜜蜂、天气、植物、材料和设计师共用同一张时间表。
works.method: First-person research through design over a season with Osmia bicornis, documenting observation, beehouse making and shared resources in the garden.
works.method_zh: 以第一人称的“通过设计做研究”，与红壁蜂（Osmia bicornis）共处一季，记录观察、蜂屋制作以及花园中的资源共享。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C2 contact zone: immediate nature

paper.title: Designing for Interdependence of Bees, Garden, Designer, and the Changing Season

works.title: Metamorphonic
works.description: Three habitats (a dome, a temple and a tower) for domestic silk moths, from egg to adult, that turn the insects' movements into improvised ambient music instead of harvesting their silk.
works.description_zh: 为家蚕（从卵到成虫）设计的三座栖所——穹顶、神殿和塔——把昆虫的活动转成即兴环境音乐，而不是收取它们的丝。
works.idea_en: Replace the use relation with a listening relation: appreciate the silkworm's uncontrollable activity rather than its silk.
works.idea_zh: 用“聆听”的关系替代“利用”的关系：欣赏蚕不可控的活动，而不是它的丝。
works.method: Sensors in handcrafted habitats track Bombyx mori movement and trigger sound; four months of cohabitation were documented through autoethnography.
works.method_zh: 手工制作的栖所中装有传感器，追踪家蚕（Bombyx mori）的活动并触发声音；四个月的共同生活以自我民族志记录。

paper.title: Metamorphonic: A Reflective Design Inquiry into Human-Silkworm Relationship

works.title: AffectiveNemo
works.description: An aquarium system that estimates a pet fish's 'observed emotion' from how it swims and shows it as speech bubbles on a screen behind the tank.
works.description_zh: 一套水族箱系统：根据鱼的游动方式估计它的“被观察到的情绪”，并在鱼缸后的屏幕上以对话气泡显示。
works.idea_en: Giving fish a readable 'voice' can keep owners engaged in their care.
works.idea_zh: 给鱼一种看得懂的“声音”，能让主人更持续地照顾它们。
works.method: Camera tracking of fish movement is combined with emotions people attribute to the fish to estimate an 'observed emotion' shown on an LCD behind the aquarium.
works.method_zh: 结合摄像头追踪的鱼类运动数据与人们赋予鱼的情绪，估计出“被观察到的情绪”，显示在鱼缸后的液晶屏上。

paper.title: AffectiveNemo: Promoting Owner-Fish Interaction by Displaying Observed Fish Emotion with Speech Bubble

works.title: TalkingNemo
works.description: An aquarium that watches its fish and water with a camera and sensors and 'speaks' for the fish in speech balloons, telling owners when something is wrong.
works.description_zh: 一个水族箱：用摄像头和传感器观察鱼和水质，并以对话气泡“替鱼说话”，在出问题时提醒主人。
works.idea_en: Translate tank conditions into the fish's first-person voice.
works.idea_zh: 把鱼缸状况翻译成鱼的第一人称话语。
works.method: Camera and water sensors detect fish condition and tank state; rules convert them into messages from the fish's perspective.
works.method_zh: 摄像头和水质传感器检测鱼的状态和缸内环境，再按规则转换成以鱼的口吻发出的消息。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 sensing the environment (text messages)

paper.title: TalkingNemo: aquarium fish talks its mind for breeding support

works.title: Silk fabricator
works.description: Silkworms placed on computer-designed 3D frames spin flat silk sheets over them instead of cocoons, producing shells such as a silk sphere or bunny.
works.description_zh: 把蚕放在计算机设计的立体框架上，它们吐出的不是茧而是覆盖框架的平面丝片，形成丝质球体、兔子等外壳。
works.idea_en: Use silkworms as 3D printers: the fabrication step is the animal's own spinning.
works.idea_zh: 把蚕当作 3D 打印机：制造这一步就是蚕自己吐丝。
works.method: Frames are designed and fabricated from 3D models; silkworms spinning on them lay down silk sheets that take the frame's shape.
works.method_zh: 根据三维模型设计并制作框架；蚕在上面吐丝，丝片便贴合框架成形。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating behaviour into sculpture

paper.title: Silk fabricator: using silkworms as 3D printers

works.title: Sensing Bodies
works.description: A triptych of interactive installations with indigo, tobacco and rice, plantation plants of the U.S. South, that pairs plant and human biodata to recall slavery and the health of tobacco field workers.
works.description_zh: 一组三联互动装置，使用靛蓝、烟草和水稻这三种美国南方种植园作物，把植物与人的生物数据并置，唤起对奴隶制和烟草田工人健康问题的记忆。
works.idea_en: Plant interfaces can carry colonial history: which plant you choose is a political decision.
works.idea_zh: 植物界面也能承载殖民历史：选择哪种植物本身就是政治决定。
works.method: Biosensors on plants and people drive data displays in three tangible, embodied encounters, framed by three postcolonial design provocations.
works.method_zh: 植物和人身上的生物传感器驱动数据显示，构成三次可触摸的具身相遇，并以三条后殖民设计“挑衅”作为框架。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C3 ethico-political provocation (colonialism and slavery)

paper.title: Sensing Bodies: Engaging Postcolonial Histories through More-than-Human Interactions

works.title: Tranquillity at Home
works.description: A plant whose grow light is set by its owner's mental fatigue, estimated from eye blinks, so the plant's health slowly mirrors the owner's wellbeing.
works.description_zh: 一盆植物的补光灯由主人的精神疲劳程度决定（通过眨眼估算），于是植物的健康会慢慢映照出主人的状态。
works.idea_en: Couple your biosignals to a plant's growth to reflect on your own wellbeing.
works.idea_zh: 把自己的生理信号和植物的生长连在一起，借此反观自身状态。
works.method: Browser-based face-landmark detection measures blink frequency; daily fatigue scores set the intensity and quality of a grow LED over the plant.
works.method_zh: 基于浏览器的人脸特征点检测测量眨眼频率；每日疲劳分数决定植物上方补光 LED 的强度与光质。

paper.title: Tranquillity at Home: Designing Plant-mediated Interaction for Fatigue Assessment

works.title: VR videos of animal vision
works.description: 360° VR videos that simulate the eyesight, colour vision and motion vision of turtles, tortoises, geckos and frogs, shown at a zoo workshop and a science festival.
works.description_zh: 模拟乌龟、陆龟、壁虎和青蛙的视力、色觉与动态视觉的 360° 虚拟现实影像，在动物园工作坊和科学节上展示。
works.idea_en: Let people try on another animal's eyes, while being honest that the simulation is approximate.
works.idea_zh: 让人“借用”另一种动物的眼睛，同时坦承这种模拟只是近似。
works.method: Footage filmed in real environments is blurred, recoloured or masked by motion detection based on scientific knowledge of each species' vision; 235 visitors answered questionnaires.
works.method_zh: 依据各物种视觉的科学知识，对实景拍摄的影像做模糊、改色或基于运动检测的遮罩处理；235 名观众填写了问卷。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 sensing beyond human senses

paper.title: Exploring the Needs and Ways to Use Virtual Reality to Understand Animals' Perceptions: A Field Study in a Science Workshop and Exhibition

works.title: BubbleTalk
works.description: A fish-tank system that turns a keeper's actions, logged on a phone, into bubbles released into the tank, so the human's presence reaches the fish.
works.description_zh: 一套鱼缸系统：把养鱼人在手机上记录的动作转成释放到缸里的气泡，让人的存在能“传到”鱼那里。
works.idea_en: Bridge the glass wall: give people a way to act into the fish's world.
works.idea_zh: 跨越玻璃壁：给人一种作用于鱼的世界的方式。
works.method: An air-pump module controlled from a smartphone app releases bubbles into the tank; a user study with guppy keepers observed how behaviour and relationships changed.
works.method_zh: 由手机应用控制的气泵模块向鱼缸释放气泡；对孔雀鱼饲养者的用户研究观察了行为与关系的变化。

paper.title: BubbleTalk: Enriching Experience with Fish by Supporting Human Behavior

works.title: I/O Plant
works.description: A toolkit that lets designers attach sensors and actuators to living plants and wire them as input/output modules in hybrid plant-electronic circuits.
works.description_zh: 一套工具包，让设计师把传感器和执行器装到活植物上，把植物当作输入/输出模块接入植物与电子混合的电路。
works.idea_en: Treat a plant as a module you can plug into interaction design.
works.idea_zh: 把植物当作可以接入交互设计的一个模块。
works.method: Sensor and actuator modules read plant biopotential and touch and drive outputs such as light and motion; the paper reports usage patterns and examples.
works.method_zh: 传感与执行模块读取植物生物电和触摸，驱动灯光、运动等输出；论文报告了使用模式和示例。

paper.title: I/O plant: a tool kit for designing augmented human-plant interactions

works.title: Plant Feeling Light
works.description: A lighting system whose colour and brightness follow the biorhythm of a living plant, read from its bioelectric signals.
works.description_zh: 一套照明系统，其颜色和亮度随活植物的生物节律变化，节律读自植物的生物电信号。
works.idea_en: Let a plant's own rhythm set the light in a room.
works.idea_zh: 让植物自身的节律来决定房间里的光。
works.method: Plant biopotential is measured and mapped by a control algorithm onto the amplitude and colour of LED panels.
works.method_zh: 测量植物生物电，并通过控制算法映射为 LED 灯板的亮度和颜色。

paper.title: Plant feeling light: a lighting system working with plant biorhythms

works.title: Living sensing systems (Winogradsky columns)
works.description: A bio-electronic device that visualises bacterial activity in Winogradsky columns filled with local soil, deployed for a month with two urban communities.
works.description_zh: 一个生物电子装置，把装着本地土壤的维诺格拉茨基柱（Winogradsky column）中的细菌活动可视化，在两个城市社区部署了一个月。
works.idea_en: Soil microbes can be slow, collective environmental sensors for a neighbourhood.
works.idea_zh: 土壤微生物可以成为一个社区缓慢而集体的环境传感器。
works.method: Electrodes measure electrical activity of microbial communities growing in soil columns; LED matrices show activity per layer and over time.
works.method_zh: 电极测量土壤柱中微生物群落的电活动，LED 点阵显示各层以及随时间变化的活动。

paper.title: Community engagements with living sensing systems

works.title: Guttation Sensor
works.description: A paper-based microfluidic chip worn on a leaf that collects guttation droplets and changes colour to show six chemicals linked to the plant's condition.
works.description_zh: 一张贴在叶片上的纸基微流控芯片，收集植物吐水的液滴，并通过变色显示与植物状况相关的六种化学物质。
works.idea_en: Read a plant's chemistry on the spot, without a lab.
works.idea_zh: 不进实验室，就地读懂植物的化学状态。
works.method: Wearable paper microfluidics with colorimetric reagents collect droplets from leaf margins; tested on tomato plants.
works.method_zh: 带比色试剂的可穿戴纸基微流控芯片从叶缘收集液滴，在番茄植株上做了测试。

paper.title: Guttation Sensor: Wearable Microfluidic Chip for Plant Condition Monitoring and Diagnosis

works.title: Towards the Plant-Based Sensor
works.description: Long-running experiments with mud and plant microbial fuel cells to power low-power circuits that sense a plant's movement responses.
works.description_zh: 用泥土与植物微生物燃料电池做的长期实验，为感知植物运动反应的低功耗电路供电。
works.idea_en: A plant-and-microbe system could power the sensor that watches it.
works.idea_zh: 植物与微生物组成的系统，也许能为监测它自己的传感器供电。
works.method: MudWatt kits and a plant-based MFC (asparagus fern) were logged for weeks; plant sensing relies on thigmonastic responses and biopotential.
works.method_zh: 对 MudWatt 套件和以文竹为基础的植物微生物燃料电池做了数周记录；植物传感依靠触发性运动和生物电。

paper.title: Towards the Plant-Based Sensor: Agricultural Energy Harvesting and Sensing Experiments

works.title: Growing Patterns
works.description: Forty textile samples dyed by living Janthinobacterium lividum, whose violet pigment is steered into intentional patterns by fibre choice, 3D printing, jacquard weaving and other surface techniques.
works.description_zh: 40 块由活的淡紫色杆菌（Janthinobacterium lividum）染色的织物样品；通过纤维选择、3D 打印、提花织造等表面工艺，引导其紫色素形成有意设计的图案。
works.idea_en: Pattern design with bacteria: control where they grow, not the colour itself.
works.idea_zh: 用细菌做图案设计：控制的是它们在哪里生长，而不是颜色本身。
works.method: Bacteria are grown directly on textiles combined with 3D-printed barriers, jacquard structures and other fibre manipulations that guide pigment deposition.
works.method_zh: 让细菌直接在织物上生长，并结合 3D 打印的阻隔层、提花结构和其他纤维处理来引导色素沉积。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating growth into textiles

paper.title: Growing Patterns: Textile Design with Living Pigments

works.title: FloraWear
works.description: DIY wearable planters (bracelets, necklaces and rings) in which seeds germinate and grow on the body; twenty people wore them for weeks.
works.description_zh: 可以自己动手做的可穿戴花器（手环、项链和戒指），种子在身上发芽生长；20 位参与者佩戴了数周。
works.idea_en: Wearing a growing plant makes the wearer part of its ecosystem.
works.idea_zh: 戴着一株正在生长的植物，人就成了它生态系统的一部分。
works.method: 3D-printed flexible holders with growing substrate host sprouts; the pictorial documents material tests, design iterations and wearers' experiences.
works.method_zh: 3D 打印的柔性容器装入栽培基质承载幼苗；这篇图文论文记录了材料测试、设计迭代和佩戴者的体验。

paper.title: FloraWear: Wearable Living Interface

works.title: Tracing slime mold
works.description: A first-person design study that traces slime mould growth by drawing its paths, placing oats on a stage dish, predicting routes and sonifying its electrical resistance.
works.description_zh: 一项第一人称设计研究：通过描画黏菌的路径、在舞台培养皿上放燕麦、预测它的路线以及把它的电阻变化转成声音来“追踪”黏菌。
works.idea_en: Tracing is a material practice that shows both the organism's ways and the designer's own habits of control.
works.idea_zh: “追踪”是一种材料实践，既呈现生物的方式，也暴露设计师自己的控制习惯。
works.method: Reflective writing accompanies visual, embodied and sonified tracings of Physarum polycephalum grown in petri dishes and a fabricated stage dish.
works.method_zh: 在培养皿和自制舞台培养皿中培养多头绒泡菌，并以反思写作配合视觉、身体和声音三种追踪方式。

paper.title: Tracing as a Strategy for Orienting to Nonhuman Perspectives

works.title: Mud Collecting Journey
works.description: A toolkit for collecting mud from the wild to set up Electric Life, Teresa van Dongen's bacteria-powered light installation at the Centre Pompidou, and a reflection on how the process shifted the designers from concern to care.
works.description_zh: 一套从野外采集泥土的工具包，用来搭建 Teresa van Dongen 在蓬皮杜中心展出的细菌供电灯光装置 Electric Life；论文同时反思了这一过程如何让设计师从“关注”转向“照护”。
works.idea_en: Slow, unpredictable microbes challenge the designer's sense of control and invite care.
works.idea_zh: 缓慢而不可预测的微生物会动摇设计师的掌控感，引出照护。
works.method: Mud from natural sites is packed into microbial fuel cells whose electroactive bacteria light LEDs; the toolkit asks the user to touch and observe the mud.
works.method_zh: 把自然场地的泥土装进微生物燃料电池，其中的产电细菌点亮 LED；工具包引导使用者触摸并观察泥土。

paper.title: From Concern to Care: A Transformative Reflection on Designing-with the Living

works.title: Bees: new creative agents
works.description: Sculptural objects whose final form is built by honeybees nesting and making comb on designed structures, proposed as a link between the creative industries and bee decline.
works.description_zh: 一组雕塑物件：蜜蜂在设计好的结构上筑巢造脾，完成物件最终的形态；作品被提出作为连接创意产业与蜜蜂减少问题的桥梁。
works.idea_en: Bees as co-makers: the design sets conditions, the colony finishes the form.
works.idea_zh: 把蜜蜂当作共同制作者：设计设定条件，蜂群完成形态。
works.method: Structures are placed in hives so that honeybees build comb on and around them (likely); the resulting forms become objects.
works.method_zh: 把结构放进蜂箱，让蜜蜂在其上及周围筑脾（推测），形成的形态即成为物件。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating nesting behaviour into sculpture

paper.title: Bees: new creative agents

works.title: Sensing More-than-human Worlds
works.description: Recordings of light and sound at Glasson Dock and Sunderland Point near Lancaster, visualised as circular charts that include ultrasound inaudible to people, to show how urban places are sensed by nonhuman life.
works.description_zh: 在兰卡斯特附近的 Glasson Dock 与 Sunderland Point 录下光与声，并做成环形图（包括人耳听不到的超声），以展示城市场所如何被非人类生命感知。
works.idea_en: Media architecture can reveal what a place is like for other species.
works.idea_zh: 媒体建筑可以揭示一个地方对其他物种来说是什么样子。
works.method: Light sensors and ultrasonic microphones recorded four-hour sessions at dusk; the data became radial visualisations, discussed within a review of more-than-human city design.
works.method_zh: 用光传感器和超声麦克风在黄昏录制四小时的数据，并做成放射状可视化，放在对超越人类城市设计的综述中讨论。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 sensing beyond human senses

paper.title: More-Than-Human Future Cities: From the design of nature to designing for and through nature

works.title: Synthium
works.description: A tangible installation for urban green spaces that turns electrical signals from living mushrooms into sound people can play with.
works.description_zh: 一件放在城市绿地的实体装置，把活蘑菇的电信号变成人们可以玩的声音。
works.idea_en: Playful sound can introduce fungi as fellow stakeholders in the city.
works.idea_zh: 用好玩的声音，把真菌介绍为城市里的利益相关者。
works.method: Electrodes read bioelectric signals from mushrooms and drive a synthesiser; the concept moved from cardboard prototypes to a mid-fidelity proof of concept through a Double Diamond process.
works.method_zh: 电极读取蘑菇的生物电信号并驱动合成器；概念经双钻石流程，从纸板原型发展到中等保真度的概念验证。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating biopotential into sound

paper.title: Synthium: Mushrooms to facilitate the transition to the Post-Anthropocene

works.title: Plant Play
works.description: An experimental videogame artwork designed for a Venus flytrap to play, with sensors wired to the plant controlling the game.
works.description_zh: 一件为捕蝇草设计的实验性电子游戏艺术作品，接在植物上的传感器控制游戏。
works.idea_en: Imagining a plant as a player unsettles what play means for humans.
works.idea_zh: 把植物想象成玩家，会动摇人类对“玩”的理解。
works.method: Sensor wiring reads the Venus flytrap's electrical signals and uses them as game input, framed by feminist and posthumanist ideas of nonhuman play.
works.method_zh: 传感线路读取捕蝇草的电信号作为游戏输入，并以女性主义和后人类主义关于非人类游戏的思想为框架。

paper.title: Plant Play

works.title: pheB
works.description: A soft robotic wall surface that inflates and deflates with a plant's internal signals and guides people in confined spaces through breathing exercises.
works.description_zh: 一面软体机器人墙面，随植物的内部信号充气和放气，引导身处封闭空间的人做呼吸练习。
works.idea_en: Feel a plant's state through a moving surface to regulate your own emotions.
works.idea_zh: 通过一面会动的表面感受植物的状态，借此调节自己的情绪。
works.method: Plant biosignals drive pneumatic soft actuators; an early user study tested guided breathing and design preferences.
works.method_zh: 植物生物信号驱动气动软体执行器；早期用户研究测试了引导呼吸效果和设计偏好。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 translating plant biopotential into shape change

paper.title: Plant-Human Embodied Biofeedback (pheB): A Soft Robotic Surface for Emotion Regulation in Confined Physical Space

works.title: 'イ'(1926) by BioLuminescent Bacteria
works.description: The katakana 'イ', the first image Kenjiro Takayanagi showed on a CRT television in 1926, silkscreen-printed onto agar with bioluminescent bacteria as ink; it glows, then fades and vanishes as the bacteria grow and die.
works.description_zh: 把片假名“イ”——高柳健次郎 1926 年在显像管电视上显示的第一个图像——用发光细菌作墨水丝网印在琼脂上；随着细菌生长和死亡，图像先发光，再衰退直至消失。
works.idea_en: An image with a lifespan: media history re-rendered in a living display.
works.idea_zh: 有寿命的图像：用活的显示媒介重演媒体史。
works.method: Digital silkscreen printing deposits luminous bacteria on agar media; the image is photographed over 12 to 48 hours as it develops.
works.method_zh: 用数字丝网印刷把发光细菌印到琼脂培养基上，在 12 至 48 小时内拍摄图像的变化。

paper.title: 'イ'(1926) by BioLuminescent Bacteria

works.title: Pudica
works.description: A design framework and prototype that close the leaves of a Mimosa pudica with electrical stimulation, so each leaf can display data such as air quality or a message from a loved one.
works.description_zh: 一套设计框架和原型：用电刺激让含羞草的叶片闭合，每片叶子都可以显示空气质量或来自亲人的讯息等数据。
works.idea_en: Plant interfaces fit emotionally strong uses best, and they need a plan for maintenance and reproducibility.
works.idea_zh: 植物界面最适合情感浓厚的用途，同时需要考虑维护和可复现性。
works.method: Electrodes trigger the thigmonastic leaf-closing response of Mimosa pudica; a user study measured affinity for plants and for the interface.
works.method_zh: 电极触发含羞草叶片受触闭合的反应；用户研究测量了人们对植物和对该界面的好感。

paper.title: Pudica: A Framework For Designing Augmented Human-Flora Interaction

works.title: Minty Zoo
works.description: A cabinet of five 'hub' mint plants given uneven water and light; 15 sensors track their collective behaviour and the data decides how resources are redistributed among them.
works.description_zh: 一个柜子里放着五株“枢纽”薄荷，水和光的分配并不均匀；15 个传感器追踪它们的集体行为，再由数据决定如何在它们之间重新分配资源。
works.idea_en: Let plants 'communicate' their needs to each other through a technical system.
works.idea_zh: 通过技术系统，让植物彼此“传达”自己的需要。
works.method: Soil moisture, temperature, humidity, CO2 and ammonia sensors plus time-lapse imaging feed rules that re-route water and light across the plants.
works.method_zh: 土壤湿度、温度、湿度、二氧化碳和氨气传感器以及延时摄影提供数据，按规则在植物之间重新分配水和光。

paper.title: Minty Zoo: An Interspecies Plant-Based Communication System

works.title: Plant listener
works.description: A sensing device placed with plants in a Rotterdam neighbourhood that reports environmental conditions to help residents make planting and gardening decisions, part of a biodiversity urban living lab.
works.description_zh: 放在鹿特丹一个社区植物旁的感测装置，报告环境状况，帮助居民决定种什么、怎么打理花园；它是一个生物多样性城市生活实验室的一部分。
works.idea_en: Bring plants and sensors into community co-design as more-than-human participants.
works.idea_zh: 把植物和传感器作为超越人类的参与者，纳入社区共创。
works.method: Research through design and action research in Oud-Mathenesse, with a pop-up teahouse, a 'Circles of Green' tool and soil and light sensing compared against plant knowledge.
works.method_zh: 在 Oud-Mathenesse 社区开展“通过设计做研究”与行动研究，包括快闪茶屋、“Circles of Green”工具，以及把土壤与光照传感数据与植物知识对照。

paper.title: Beyond human sensors: More-than-human Citizen Sensing in biodiversity Urban Living Labs

works.title: Smart Bee Houses
works.description: Three houses for solitary mason bees with environmental sensors, colour-coded nesting tubes and modular parts, designed to support urban pollinators and record climate data.
works.description_zh: 三座为独居壁蜂设计的蜂屋，配有环境传感器、按颜色区分的巢管和模块化部件，用来支持城市传粉者并记录气候数据。
works.idea_en: Design for bees first, and ask whether the digital layer is needed at all.
works.idea_zh: 先为蜜蜂设计，再追问数字层是否真的必要。
works.method: Wood and cardboard nesting tubes are paired with Arduino-based temperature and humidity sensing; the paper reflects on materials and outdoor constraints.
works.method_zh: 木头和纸板巢管搭配基于 Arduino 的温湿度传感；论文反思了材料与户外条件带来的限制。

paper.title: Smart Bee Houses: Designing to Support Urban Pollination

works.title: Printable Hydroponics
works.description: A technique that 3D prints a plastic landscape and places seeds at set positions on it, so that with water, light and nutrients it grows into a hydroponic garden.
works.description_zh: 一种技术：3D 打印出塑料地景，并把种子自动放到预设位置，加上水、光和营养液后就长成一座水培花园。
works.idea_en: Print ecological systems, not only objects.
works.idea_zh: 打印生态系统，而不只是物件。
works.method: Multi-material printing produces porous plastic structures with seed pockets that wick nutrient solution; plants germinate and grow on the print.
works.method_zh: 多材料打印生成带种子槽的多孔塑料结构，能吸引营养液；植物在打印件上发芽生长。

paper.title: Printable Hydroponics: Digital Fabrication of Ecological Systems

works.title: Calmbots
works.description: Groups of three to five cockroaches with small electronic backpacks are steered by electrical stimulation toward goals, where they draw, carry objects, form displays or give haptic feedback.
works.description_zh: 三到五只背着小型电子背包的蟑螂组成小队，通过电刺激被引导到目标位置，用来绘画、搬运物品、组成显示或提供触觉反馈。
works.idea_en: Living insects as a swarm interface for creative work.
works.idea_zh: 把活昆虫当作用于创作的群体界面。
works.method: AR markers on the backpacks are tracked by a camera; a radio base station sends stimulation to steer each insect, with at least 60% reaching accuracy.
works.method_zh: 摄像头追踪背包上的 AR 标记，无线基站发送刺激信号引导每只昆虫，到达目标的准确率至少为 60%。

paper.title: Calmbots: Exploring Possibilities of Multiple Insects with On-hand Devices and Flexible Controls as Creation Interfaces

works.title: Turner Boxes
works.description: Folded cardboard camera boxes placed in urban gardens that photograph wild bees at times predicted from weather data, designed with beekeepers and ecologists.
works.description_zh: 放在城市花园里的折叠纸板相机盒，在根据天气数据预测的时段拍摄野蜂；与养蜂人和生态学家一起设计。
works.idea_en: Ambivalence about intervening in bee ecologies is a resource for multispecies design.
works.idea_zh: 对是否干预蜜蜂生态的矛盾心态，本身就是多物种设计的资源。
works.method: Cameras triggered by weather-based predictions of bee activity collect images to train a model; design choices on EMF, sucrose feeding and intervention are analysed through feminist diffraction.
works.method_zh: 相机根据天气预测的蜜蜂活跃时段触发拍摄，图像用于训练模型；论文借女性主义的“衍射”概念分析关于电磁场、糖水喂食和干预程度的设计选择。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C2 contact zone: immediate nature

paper.title: Turner Boxes and Bees: From Ambivalence to Diffraction

works.title: Prototyping biotic games with JavaScript
works.description: An online IDE and JavaScript API for writing games and interactive experiments that control swarms of live Euglena in remote microscopes in real time.
works.description_zh: 一个在线编程环境和 JavaScript API，用来编写能实时控制远程显微镜中活眼虫群的游戏和互动实验。
works.idea_en: Make living cells programmable over the web like any other interactive medium.
works.idea_zh: 让活细胞像其他交互媒介一样，能通过网络编程。
works.method: Cloud-connected microscopes image microfluidic chips of Euglena gracilis; the API exposes cell tracking and LED light stimuli to user code.
works.method_zh: 联网显微镜拍摄装有纤细眼虫（Euglena gracilis）的微流控芯片；API 向用户代码开放细胞追踪和 LED 光刺激。

paper.title: Prototyping Biotic Games and Interactive Experiments with JavaScript

works.title: Sloooooooooow
works.description: An IoT home installation in which smart curtains open and close with the humidity that three plants transpire, changing the sunlight that reaches them.
works.description_zh: 一个物联网家居装置：智能窗帘随三株植物蒸腾带来的湿度变化而开合，从而改变照到它们身上的阳光。
works.idea_en: Design for the shared microclimate instead of the single plant: a plant-decentred view.
works.idea_zh: 为共享的微气候设计，而不是为单株植物设计：一种“去植物中心”的视角。
works.method: Humidity sensors detect transpiration; the readings synchronise curtain movement, and time-lapse footage makes the plants' slowness visible.
works.method_zh: 湿度传感器检测蒸腾作用，读数同步驱动窗帘运动，延时摄影让植物的缓慢变得可见。
keywords: Ikeya 2025: C1 automated action to change the environment

paper.title: Slowing Plants, Slowing Home: Proposing A Plant-Decentred Perspective to Human-Plant Interaction

works.title: Whispers from Silken Margins
works.description: A gallery installation of flat silk sheets spun by silkworms, reviving a Showa-era technique in which the worm spins a plane instead of a cocoon, arranged after Archimedean solids.
works.description_zh: 一件画廊装置，由蚕吐出的平面丝片组成；它复兴了昭和时期让蚕吐出平面而不是结茧的技术，并按阿基米德多面体来组织形态。
works.idea_en: Flat cocoons keep the silkworm alive and open a new spatial vocabulary for silk.
works.idea_zh: 平面茧让蚕得以存活，也为丝打开了新的空间语言。
works.method: Silkworms spin on flat frames producing sheets of 16 different textures and fibre structures, which are assembled into polyhedral forms.
works.method_zh: 蚕在平面框架上吐丝，得到 16 种不同质感和纤维结构的丝片，再组装成多面体形态。

paper.title: Whispers from Silken Margins: Crafting Subtle Narratives in Silk-Defined Spaces

works.title: MossWater
works.description: A living moss display on the desk that is watered each time an office worker drinks, so the moss's condition shows how well the person is hydrating.
works.description_zh: 桌上的一块活苔藓显示器：办公室员工每喝一次水，苔藓就被浇一次水，于是苔藓的状态反映了这个人喝水是否充足。
works.idea_en: Caring for moss becomes a metaphor for caring for one's own health.
works.idea_zh: 照料苔藓成了照顾自身健康的隐喻。
works.method: A cup sensor detects drinking and triggers a pump and fan module that water and ventilate the moss; a user study examined usability and empathy.
works.method_zh: 杯子上的传感器检测饮水动作，触发水泵和风扇模块为苔藓浇水、通风；用户研究考察了可用性和共情反应。

paper.title: MossWater: A Living Media Interface for Encouraging Office Workers' Daily Water Intake
